Custom CRM Updates Code Guide

Every change made to the Lead, Opportunity and Project Tender in the custom_crm_updates app: what it does, how it was programmed, and the real code with its line numbers.

App
apps/custom_crm_updates
Platform
ERPNext v14 · Frappe v14
Steps
25
Functions
60 Python · 14 JavaScript
Server code
1615 lines in 7 files
Companion
docs/custom-crm-updates.html

How to read this guide

Part 1 explains the five Frappe tools everything is built from. Part 2 shows how the files connect. Part 3 walks through the work step by step, in the order it was built: for each step, what it does for users, why it was built that way, the actual code (copied from the files when this guide was generated, with real line numbers), and an explanation. Parts 4 and 5 are look-up tables.

Part 1

Frappe building blocks

Every change in this guide uses one of these few tools. Read this once and the rest of the code reads easily.

ToolWhat it isHow we used it
DocTypeA record type: its fields are stored in a JSON file, its rules in a Python class (the "controller").New: Leads Activity and 4 child tables.
Child tableA DocType with istable: 1. Its rows live inside a parent document, shown as a grid.Attachments, the activity / tender / contact tables.
Custom FieldA field added to an existing DocType (Lead, Opportunity) without editing ERPNext's files.Is Company, Customer Group, new tabs, sections and tables.
Property SetterChanges one property of an existing field (hidden, label, options, mandatory…) or the field order.Hide person fields, new Opportunity statuses, section order.
hooks.pyThe app's wiring file. Frappe reads it to know which of our functions to call and when.doc_events, doctype_js, after_migrate, override_doctype_dashboards.
Form scriptJavaScript that runs inside a form in the browser: buttons, menus, field behaviour.Create ▸ Activity, New Activity / New Contact buttons.
bench migrateApplies DocType JSON changes to the database, then runs the after_migrate hooks.Re-creates all custom fields and property setters, fills the tables.

When our code runs during a save

Frappe calls a fixed series of methods every time a document is saved. doc_events in hooks.py attach our functions to these moments; a DocType's own controller can define them as methods. Highlighted boxes are where this app plugs in.

before_validateLead: clear person fields
→
validateLead: require group + territory; Lead/Opp: refresh Contacts
→
database writerow saved
→
on_updateActivity: automations; Contact / Tender: sync tables
→
after_insertnew records only (Lead: contacts)

Deleting runs on_trash first, before Frappe checks whether other records still link to the one being deleted. That ordering is used three times in this app (Sheet steps 06, 11, 14).

Words used in the code

doc / selfThe document being saved (a Python object with one attribute per field).
get_doc_before_save()A copy of the document as it was in the database before this save; None when the document is new. Used to detect "status changed to Done".
db_set()Writes field values straight to the database without running the document's validations.
frappe.get_all()Database query returning a list of rows, ignoring permissions.
frappe.throw()Stops the save, rolls back everything done in it, and shows the message to the user.
add_comment("Info", …)Adds a line to the record's timeline, so users can see why something changed.
idempotentSafe to run again: running twice gives the same result as once. All setup code is written this way.

How the files fit together

hooks.py is the switchboard. It routes events from ERPNext records to our modules; the modules then read and write those records. Everything lives in apps/custom_crm_updates/custom_crm_updates/.

FileTypeResponsible for

overrides/contact.pyPythonContacts tables on Lead and Opportunity

custom_crm_updates/doctype/leads_activity/DocTypeThe activity record, its automations, list colours, form script, tests
custom_crm_updates/doctype/…_detail, …_attachment, opportunity_project_tenderDocType (child)Row layouts for the tables
public/js/lead.js, opportunity.jsJavaScriptForm controllers: Create menu, buttons

Part 3

Step by step

25 steps, in the order they were built. Files are relative to apps/custom_crm_updates/custom_crm_updates/.

01

Is Company hides the person fields

When a Lead represents a company, the person fields (salutation, first/middle/last name, gender, job title) disappear, and they are cleared when saved.

overrides/lead.pyhooks.py → before_validate
Why this wayNo ERPNext file is edited. Visibility is a property setter (depends_on) on each person field, so the form hides them instantly; clearing the values is a before_validate hook so stale names never reach the saved Lead. This part already existed in the app when the work started and is explained here for completeness.
  1. depends_on = "eval: !doc.custom_is_company" is a tiny JavaScript expression the form evaluates on every change: the field shows only while Is Company is unticked.
  2. Core ERPNext makes First Name mandatory whenever Organization Name is empty. With First Name hidden, that would demand a field the user cannot see, so mandatory_depends_on flips the rule: a company requires Organization Name instead.
  3. clear_person_fields runs before ERPNext's own validate. It empties the person fields and sets lead_name (Full Name) to the company name, because ERPNext only fills lead_name when it is empty.
02

Organization section before Contact Info

The Organization block moves up so it sits right after the main details.

overrides/lead.py → apply_field_order, move_section
Why this wayERPNext's own fields cannot be moved with insert_after (that only works for custom fields). The only supported way is a field_order property setter: the full list of fieldnames in display order, exactly what Customize Form saves when you drag fields. We rebuild that list in code so it is reapplied on every migrate.
  1. frappe.get_meta("Lead", cached=False).fields gives every field in its current display order, including custom fields.
  2. move_section finds the section's first field, walks forward until the next Section Break or Tab Break, cuts that block out, and inserts it before the target field. Example: [type, CONTACT_INFO, email, phone, ORGANIZATION, company_name, fax, ADDRESS] becomes [type, ORGANIZATION, company_name, fax, CONTACT_INFO, email, phone, ADDRESS].
  3. The optional header is a field (the new Tab Break, step 8) that is placed in front of the moved block.
  4. If the new order equals the current one, nothing is written. That makes the function idempotent: running it on every migrate is safe, and any other ordering someone saved in Customize Form is kept.
03

The Leads Activity DocType

A new record type for every touchpoint: type, status, date, who is responsible, what it is linked to, and files.

leads_activity.jsonleads_activity_attachment.jsonleads_activity.jsleads_activity_list.js
Why this wayA DocType is defined by its JSON file; bench migrate creates the database table from it. The Link field has to point at Lead, Prospect or Opportunity, so it is a Dynamic Link: its target DocType is read from another field (link_type).

Fields (read from the JSON file)

FieldnameLabelTypeOptionsFlags
activity_typeTypeSelectCall, Meeting, Site Visit, Registration, Tendering, Otherreqd, in_list_view
statusStatusSelectPlanned, In Process, Done, Failed, Closed, Waiting Replyreqd, in_list_view
dateDateDatereqd, in_list_view
assigned_toAssigned ToLinkUser
assigned_to_nameAssigned To NameDataread_only
link_typeLink TypeSelectLead, Prospect, Opportunityreqd, in_list_view
link_nameLinkDynamic Linklink_typereqd, in_list_view
attachmentsAttachmentsTableLeads Activity Attachment
  1. "options": "link_type" makes it dynamic: Frappe reads the value of link_type ("Lead") and lists Leads, validates the value exists, and shows it as a clickable link.
  2. Because Frappe knows about this dynamic link, it refuses to delete a Lead that still has activities. That integrity comes for free.
  3. Records are named CRM-ACT-.YYYY.-.##### (the JSON autoname), e.g. CRM-ACT-2026-00001.
  4. Attachments is a Table field whose rows are the child DocType Leads Activity Attachment (an Attach field and a description), so any number of files can be added.
  1. frappe.ui.form.on("Leads Activity", {...}) registers handlers for this form. A handler named after a field runs when that field changes.
  2. link_type(frm): when Link Type changes, the old Link points at the wrong kind of record, so it is cleared.
  3. set_query("assigned_to", …) limits Assigned To to enabled system users.
  1. listview_settings[…].get_indicator returns [label, colour, filter] for each row; Frappe draws the coloured status pill in the list, and clicking it filters by that status.
04

Activities drive the Lead's qualification

A new Registration activity sets the Lead to In Process; any activity reaching Done sets it to Qualified.

leads_activity.py → LeadsActivity.on_update, set_lead_qualification
Why this wayThe rule belongs to the activity, so it lives in the activity's own controller (class LeadsActivity), in on_update, which Frappe calls after every save. The Lead is updated with db_set, not a full save, so a salesperson without edit rights on the Lead can still log activities, and an unrelated problem on the Lead (for example a duplicate email) cannot block recording the activity.
  1. before = self.get_doc_before_save() is None for a brand-new activity. So before is None means "just created".
  2. Registration rule: only on creation, and skip_if=("In Process", "Qualified") means a Lead that is already further along is never moved back.
  3. became_done is true when the status is Done now and was not Done before (or the activity is new, or it was moved to another Lead). Re-saving a Done activity therefore does nothing.
  4. set_lead_qualification also fills Qualified By (the activity's Assigned To, or the current user) and Qualified On (today).
  5. db_set(values, notify=True) writes the fields and tells any browser that has this Lead open to reload it. add_comment writes the timeline line "Qualification Status set to Qualified by CRM-ACT-…".
  6. The Tendering and Registration-to-Customer parts of on_update are explained in steps 10 and 13.
05

Create ▸ Activity (and no Prospect)

On the Lead, the Create menu loses Prospect and gains Activity, which opens a new activity already linked to the Lead.

public/js/lead.jspublic/js/leads_activity_section.jshooks.py → doctype_js
Why this wayERPNext builds the Lead's Create menu inside its controller class erpnext.LeadController. Frappe runs handlers registered with frappe.ui.form.on before that class's refresh, so a normal handler would try to remove Prospect before it exists. The solution is to subclass ERPNext's controller and run our code after super.refresh().
  1. hooks.py → doctype_js appends our files after ERPNext's own Lead script, so erpnext.LeadController already exists when ours runs.
  2. class … extends erpnext.LeadController inherits everything; super.setup() / super.refresh() run ERPNext's version first.
  3. extend_cscript(cur_frm.cscript, new …) is the same call ERPNext uses to install its controller; calling it again installs ours in its place.
  4. remove_custom_button("Prospect", "Create") removes the menu item ERPNext just added.
  1. make_activity creates an unsaved Leads Activity in the browser, sets Link Type and Link from the current form, and opens it. Values are set directly, so the "Link Type changed → clear Link" handler of step 3 does not fire.
  2. setup_activity_make_method registers the same function for the Connections tab's "+" button, because Frappe's default cannot fill a Dynamic Link.
  3. add_activity_buttons adds Create ▸ Activity and the grid's New Activity button, only for saved records and only if the user may create activities.
06

Activities shown as a real table

The Lead's Activities tab gets a standard ERPNext grid listing its activities, with the ⚙ column settings.

Leads Activity Detail (child DocType)leads_activity.py → sync_activity_table…mirror_table.py
Why this wayA child table needs its rows stored inside the parent. So the activities are mirrored: whenever an activity changes, the affected Lead's table is rebuilt from the activities. This pattern (a read-only mirror table) is reused for Opportunity activities, Project Tenders and Contacts, so the writing part is in one shared module.
  1. Three custom fields: a labelled Section Break, the Table (rows of Leads Activity Detail), and a second, unlabelled Section Break so ERPNext's own Open Tasks/Events stay outside our section.
  2. read_only: 1: users cannot edit rows. no_copy: 1: Duplicate does not copy them.
  1. sync_activity_table queries every activity linked to the Lead (ascending by creation, so a new one is appended at the bottom and a back-dated one does not jump to the top) plus a count of each one's attachments, then hands the rows to set_mirror_rows.
  2. linked_docs returns the current link and the previous one when an activity is moved to another record, so the old record loses the row and the new one gains it.
  3. on_trash passes exclude=self.name: the row is removed before Frappe's link check, otherwise the row itself (a Link to the activity) would block the deletion.
  1. rows_differ compares old and new rows as strings, so a date loaded from the database equals the same date from a query. If nothing changed, nothing is written.
  2. update_child_table writes only the child rows (no full save of the Lead, so none of its validations run).
  3. bump_modified: updating the Lead's modified timestamp means a copy of the Lead that is open in someone's browser can no longer be saved over the new rows (Frappe refuses with "document has been modified"), and notify=True reloads it.
  1. backfill_activity_tables runs after every migrate and syncs every record that has activities, for activities created before the table existed. Thanks to rows_differ it touches nothing that is already correct.
  2. add_to_dashboard adds Leads Activity to the Connections tab: count by link_name, filtered by link_type. It is registered per DocType through override_doctype_dashboards.
07

Opportunity gets its own activities

The same table on the Opportunity, listing only activities whose Link Type is Opportunity.

leads_activity.py → TABLE_DOCTYPESoverrides/opportunity.pypublic/js/opportunity.js
Why this wayBecause step 6 was written around a list of DocTypes, extending it was one word: TABLE_DOCTYPES = ("Lead", "Opportunity"). The same table fieldname on both, the same child DocType, the same sync. Separation is automatic: the query filters on link_type = the record's own DocType.
  1. get_dashboard_data is the Opportunity's twin of the Lead's (step 6): it adds Leads Activity to the Opportunity's Connections tab.
  2. The Opportunity controller is subclassed exactly like the Lead's (step 5). ERPNext's Opportunity class has no setup, hence super.setup?.() (call it only if it exists).
  3. An Opportunity made from a Lead does not inherit the Lead's activity rows: ERPNext's Lead → Opportunity mapping never copies table fields.
08

Address & Contacts in its own tab

The address/contact section moves out of the Details tab into a new tab before Activities.

overrides/lead.py → ADDRESS_TAB, move_section(header=…), ADDRESS_SECTION_PROPERTIES
Why this wayA Tab Break swallows every field after it up to the next tab. Dropping one in front of the address section would also drag Qualification and Additional Information into the new tab. So the address block is first moved to just before the Activities tab, with the new Tab Break placed in front of it (the header argument of move_section).
  1. Inside its own tab the section no longer needs its heading (the tab already says it), and collapsible would open the tab with the section folded, so both are switched off with property setters.
  2. The order is applied by apply_field_order from step 2: move_section(…, "address_section", before="activities_tab", header=ADDRESS_TAB).
09

Tendering type and two new Opportunity statuses

Activity Type gains Tendering; Opportunity Status gains Tendering and Won.

leads_activity.jsonoverrides/opportunity.py → apply_opportunity_customizations
Why this wayLeads Activity is our own DocType, so its option list is edited directly in its JSON file. Opportunity belongs to ERPNext, so its Status options are changed with a property setter. The setter is built from ERPNext's original list plus ours, so options ERPNext adds in a future upgrade are kept.
  1. frappe.db.get_value("DocField", …, "options") reads ERPNext's original options (the DocField table), not the already-customized ones, so running this again never adds duplicates.
  2. ERPNext only recalculates an Opportunity's status when a Quotation is made, ordered or lost, so Tendering and Won stay put through normal saves.
  3. create_custom_fields(CUSTOM_FIELDS, update=True) creates or updates every Opportunity custom field (steps 7, 11, 14); HIDDEN_FIELDS is explained in step 14.
10

Tendering activity creates a Project Tender

Saving a Tendering activity on an Opportunity creates one Project Tender named after it, and moves the Opportunity to Tendering.

leads_activity.py → on_updateoverrides/project_tender.py
Why this wayProject Tender belongs to the contracting app, which we do not modify. Two read-only custom fields added from our app link each tender back to its Opportunity and to the activity that created it. That link is also how "one tender per activity" is guaranteed: before creating, we check whether a tender already points at this activity.
  1. The import sits inside the function (a local import) so the two modules can call each other without a circular import at load time.
  2. frappe.db.exists("Project Tender", {ACTIVITY_FIELD: activity.name}): if a tender already exists for this activity, stop. Saving the activity again never creates a second one; a new Tendering activity creates a new one.
  3. Project Name = the Opportunity's title (falling back to customer name, then its ID).
  4. insert(ignore_permissions=True): Sales Users have no Project Tender role, but the automation must still work for them.
  5. The Opportunity moves to Tendering unless it is already Won or Converted, and a timeline comment records which activity created which tender.
  6. frappe.msgprint then tells whoever saved the activity that the tender was created, with a link to it — the activity's own form would otherwise show nothing.
  7. apply_project_tender_customizations does nothing if the contracting app is missing, so the app still installs cleanly without it.
  1. Project Tender's Client is a mandatory link to a Customer. An Opportunity for a Customer uses it directly.
  2. An Opportunity for a Lead converts that Lead first (step 13), or reuses the Customer already made from it.
  3. An Opportunity for a Prospect: Customer has no link back to a Prospect, but ERPNext's own conversion names the Customer after the Prospect, so we match on that name and only create a new Customer if none exists.
  4. If the Customer cannot be created (missing Customer Group/Territory), frappe.throw cancels the whole activity save, so no half-created tender is left behind.
11

The Opportunity's Project Tender tab

A new tab between Items and Activities lists every tender created for the Opportunity.

overrides/opportunity.py → CUSTOM_FIELDSoverrides/project_tender.py → on_update, sync_opportunity_tenders…Opportunity Project Tender (child DocType)
Why this waySame mirror-table pattern as the activities (step 6). Here the source records are Project Tenders, so the sync is triggered by a doc_event on Project Tender in hooks.py: our on_update runs after the contracting app's own.
  1. insert_after: "total": the last field of the Items tab, so the new tab appears right before Activities. depends_on: "eval:!doc.__islocal" hides the tab on an unsaved Opportunity.
  2. on_update syncs both the current Opportunity and the previous one if the link changed (the before copy), then checks for Submitted (step 12). skip_opportunity_sync is the one case it skips: step 18, where the Opportunity is mid-save and refreshes its own table.
  3. tender_rows orders by creation asc: oldest tender at the top, each new one appended at the bottom. Every table in this module uses that one rule.
  4. "date(creation) as creation_date" asks the database for just the date part of when the tender was created.
  5. backfill_opportunity_tenders fills the table after a migrate for tenders that already exist.
12

A tender can only be Submitted when it is costed, and then its activity is Done

A Project Tender needs rows in all three cost tables before it can be Submitted; once it is, the activity that created it is marked Done. The Opportunity is left alone.

overrides/project_tender.py → validate_submitted_rows, mark_activity_donehooks.py → Project Tender validate
Why this waySubmitting a tender means sending a price to the client, so the costing has to be there: Direct Cost, Indirect Cost and Overhead / Deduction all need at least one row. The check sits in validate rather than on the status change alone, so emptying a table on an already-submitted tender is refused too. Whether the Opportunity is Won is a separate, human decision — several tenders can be submitted for one Opportunity and only one of them wins (step 18).
  1. The message names the tables that are still empty, using their own labels, instead of failing on whichever field the user reaches first.
  2. doc.has_value_changed("status") (in on_update, step 11) is true only on the save where the status actually changes, so re-saving a Submitted tender does not touch the activity again.
  3. The activity gets a full save (not db_set) so its own on_update runs too and the Opportunity's activities table shows Done.
  4. mark_activity_done returns early if there is nothing to do (no linked activity, or already Done). activity.flags.ignore_permissions = True: whoever submits the tender may not have rights on activities.
  5. Saving the activity re-runs its on_update; the Tendering check there finds the existing tender and does not create another.
13

Registration Done → the Lead becomes a Customer

When a Registration activity on a Lead is Done, the Lead is converted to a Customer using its own Customer Group and Territory.

leads_activity.py → on_updateoverrides/lead.py → convert_lead_to_customer, insert_customer
Why this wayWe reuse ERPNext's own Lead → Customer mapping (_make_customer), the same code behind the Lead's Create ▸ Customer button. It copies the Lead's details and, when the Customer is saved, links the Lead's contacts and addresses to it and marks the Lead Converted. We only fill in what the mapping leaves out.
  1. The trigger fires when a Registration activity becomes Done, or a Done activity is changed to Registration.
  2. frappe.db.get_value("Customer", {"lead_name": lead}): ERPNext stores the source Lead on the Customer, so an already-converted Lead is never converted twice.
  3. The mapping copies Territory (same field name on both) but takes Customer Group from the Selling Settings default; the Lead's own Customer Group (step 16) overrides it.
  4. insert_customer checks both fields first and throws a clear message naming what is missing and where to set it, instead of ERPNext's bare "mandatory field" error.
14

Contacts shown as a table

On Lead, Opportunity and Customer, ERPNext's contact list is replaced by a read-only Contacts table with a New Contact button.

overrides/contact.pyoverrides/customer.pyLeads Contact Detail (child DocType)hooks.py → Lead, Opportunity, Customer, Contact events
Why this wayContacts are linked to records through rows in the Contact's links table (Dynamic Links). An Opportunity lists the contacts linked to it and only those, so a deal's contact list is not diluted by the Lead's, and a Customer likewise lists only its own, so a contact added to the client after the sale stays out of the deal it came from. A Lead lists its own and those of every Opportunity made from it and those of the Customer it became, so the Lead stays the full picture of who is involved. The table is a mirror of those links, kept current from two directions: the record recomputes its own table whenever it is saved, and a Contact pushes its rows to every record it is (or was) linked to whenever the Contact is saved or deleted. Because the record recomputes on its own save, a stale form cannot leave wrong rows, so this table does not need the modified-timestamp bump.
  1. filters=[["Dynamic Link", "link_doctype", "=", …], …] is a child-table filter: Contacts that have a link row pointing at the given record.
  2. contact_sources decides where the rows come from: one source for an Opportunity and for a Customer, and for a Lead itself plus each of its Opportunities (oldest first) and then its Customer. A contact linked to more than one is listed once, under the first source that has it.
  3. A Customer counts as the Lead's whether it carries From Lead or From Opportunity — the two ways ERPNext records the same conversion — so the roll-up holds however the Customer was created.
  4. ERPNext's own Lead → Customer conversion links the Lead's contacts to the Customer as well, so those are the Customer's contacts too and show on both. On the Lead each one is still listed once, under the Lead.
  5. Ascending by creation, like every table here: oldest at the top, a new contact appended at the bottom. The primary contact is shown by its own column rather than sorted to the top. linked_via names the record each row came from.
  6. order_by="`tabContact`.…" names the table explicitly because the Dynamic Link join also has a creation column.
  1. refresh_own_table (Lead, Opportunity and Customer validate) sets the rows on the document being saved, so they are written with it.
  2. refresh_after_insert: ERPNext links a new Lead's auto-created contact in its after_insert, after validate has run, so we refresh once more and write the rows.
  3. affected_docs turns a contact's links into the records to update: the Leads, Opportunities and Customers it is linked to, plus the Lead behind each of those, which rolls their contacts up.
  4. lead_of reads that Lead from the database; lead_in reads it from a document in hand, which is the only way to get it from the version before a save and from one being deleted.
  5. refresh_party_lead (Opportunity and Customer on_update / on_trash) keeps the Lead level when one appears, is re-pointed at another Lead, or is deleted - the contact itself never changed, so no Contact event would fire. Both Leads are refreshed on a re-point: the one it left and the one it joined.
  6. backfill_contact_tables also syncs every record that already has rows, which is what drops the party contacts the Opportunities mirrored before the two were separated.
  7. on_contact_update merges links before and after the save, so unlinking a contact removes its row from the old record.
  1. The Customer gets the same two custom fields from the same helper, inserted after its own contact_html, i.e. at the end of the Address and Contact section of the Contact & Address tab.
  2. ERPNext's own contact list (contact_html) is hidden by a property setter on all three DocTypes. ERPNext still renders into it, just unseen, so nothing in its code breaks.
  3. The New Contact button is frappe.new_doc("Contact"), like ERPNext's. The Contact form fills its Links table from frappe.dynamic_link, so we set that to this record first: on an Opportunity, ERPNext had left its party there, which would have created the contact on the Lead instead. On a Customer this is what keeps a contact added there out of the Opportunity it came from.
  4. public/js/customer.js calls the same two helpers as the Lead and the Opportunity (show_when_empty in setup, add_contact_button in refresh), so leads_activity_section.js is loaded ahead of it in doctype_js.
15

Empty tables stay visible

A table with no rows yet (and its New Activity / New Contact button) stays on screen.

public/js/leads_activity_section.js → show_when_empty
Why this wayFrappe hides any read-only field that has no value. An empty read-only table therefore disappeared, taking its button with it (and the whole Project Tender tab, which has nothing else in it). Each field's control decides its visibility in a method called get_status; we wrap that method for our tables only.
  1. get_status returns "Write", "Read" or "None" (hidden). Our wrapper calls the original first.
  2. Only when the original says "None" and the field is not hidden on purpose, the record is saved, and the user can read it, the answer becomes "Read": shown, still read-only.
  3. It is installed in the controller's setup, which runs once per form; the controls are reused when switching between records.
16

Customer Group and Territory mandatory on Lead

A new Customer Group field beside Territory; both must be filled before a Lead can be saved, and the Customer inherits them.

overrides/lead.py → CUSTOMER_FIELDS, MANDATORY_DEPENDS_ON, validate_customer_fields
Why this wayThe obvious switch, reqd, is enforced on every insert. ERPNext also creates Leads by itself (website contact form, an Opportunity made from an email address, appointments) with nobody to ask, and those would start failing. So the form is made mandatory with mandatory_depends_on: "eval:1" (always true), and a server check covers people saving by API or import while letting ERPNext's own inserts through.
  1. In Frappe v14, mandatory_depends_on is checked by the form only (red asterisk, "Missing Fields" dialog), never by the server.
  2. validate_customer_fields runs on the server for every Lead save. ERPNext's automatic inserts pass ignore_permissions or ignore_mandatory; those are skipped. Everyone else gets the same error the form shows.
  3. Customer Group is placed right after Territory (insert_after: "territory"). Step 13 copies both into the Customer.
17

Wiring: hooks.py and the setup functions

How Frappe finds all of the above, and how it is re-applied on every migrate.

hooks.pyoverrides/lead.py → apply_lead_customizations
Why this wayAll layout changes (custom fields, property setters, field order) are created by code, not by clicking in Customize Form. That makes them repeatable on any site: bench migrate runs the after_migrate list in order, and every function in it is idempotent.
  1. doctype_js: a list per DocType; the shared helper is loaded before the form's controller so its functions exist when the controller runs.
  2. after_migrate: the three setup functions first (they create the fields), then the three backfills (they fill the tables).
  3. doc_events: dotted paths to our functions. Frappe calls each one with (doc, method); a list runs in order.
  4. override_doctype_dashboards: lets us add Leads Activity to ERPNext's Connections tab without editing ERPNext.
  1. create_custom_fields(…, update=True) creates missing fields and updates existing ones.
  2. make_property_setter replaces any existing setter for the same field and property, so re-running never duplicates.
  3. OBSOLETE_CUSTOM_FIELDS removes the HTML field used by the very first version of the activities section, replaced by the table in step 6.
18

Won Opportunity → the approved tender

Setting an Opportunity to Won opens a popup listing its Project Tenders; the one the user picks becomes Won when the Opportunity is saved.

public/js/opportunity.jsoverrides/project_tender.py → apply_approved_tender…overrides/opportunity.py → CUSTOM_FIELDShooks.py → Opportunity validate, on_update
Why this wayOne Opportunity can have several Project Tenders, so submitting one cannot decide which was approved — only the user knows, and the moment they know is when they close the Opportunity as Won. The popup therefore asks at exactly that point, and the answer is kept in a read-only field (Approved Project Tender) so the whole thing is one ordinary save: picking a tender in a dialog and writing it straight to the database would change the Opportunity under the form that is still open, and the user's own save would then be refused as out of date.
  1. The status handler fires on every change of the field. Only a change to Won on a saved Opportunity opens the popup.
  2. get_opportunity_tenders is asked for the list rather than reading the mirror table, so it is the database's answer, and it is read as the system: Project Tender is a contracting DocType the Sales User closing the Opportunity has no role on.
  3. The Select's options are {value, label} pairs: the value is the tender's ID, the label adds project name, status and total sell price so the user can tell them apart. The popup's own text is Arabic; names and status values stay English.
  4. Dismissing the popup (Esc, ✕) puts the Status back to what it was — remember_status keeps that value, because a field handler is not told the old one. A Won with nothing behind it is never left on screen.
  5. No tenders at all (a direct award): a message says so and the Won stands.
  1. apply_approved_tender (Opportunity on_update) acts only when the status is Won and something actually changed, so re-saving a Won Opportunity does not re-win anything.
  2. set_tender_won saves the tender in full, as the system, so the contracting app's own Won automation (its Project and Sales Order) runs exactly as if someone had set it by hand. Anything that automation refuses rolls the whole save back, Opportunity included, rather than leaving a Won Opportunity whose approved tender never got there.
  3. refresh_tender_rows rewrites the Opportunity's tender table through the document being saved and without the modified bump: the form that is saving would otherwise come back one step behind the database and refuse its next save. The tender is saved with skip_opportunity_sync so the usual sync does not do it the other way.
  4. validate_approved_tender guards the field against a save made over the API, where nothing has filtered the list.
  5. The other tenders are left exactly as they are: losing a tender is not the same as cancelling it.
19

Every activity on a Lead or an Opportunity needs an attachment

The Attachments table is marked mandatory as soon as the Link Type is Lead or Opportunity, or the Type is Registration, and saving without a file is refused.

leads_activity.json → attachmentsleads_activity.js → validateleads_activity.py → LeadsActivity.validate
Why this wayWhat the CRM follows a client up with is its paperwork, so an activity on a Lead or an Opportunity with nothing on file is not a record of anything — whatever its type. A Registration needs one whatever it is linked to, a Prospect included, because it is the activity that converts the Lead into a Customer (step 13), so the document it was registered with has to be on file. Three layers, each doing what only it can: mandatory_depends_on on the table puts the red asterisk there the moment the Type or the Link Type calls for it (reqd could not, because the rule depends on other fields); the form's validate refuses the save with our own message; and the server's validate is the one that actually holds, for the API and Data Import as well as the form.
  1. Frappe v14 evaluates mandatory_depends_on on the form only (layout.js turns it into reqd on every field change), which is why the server check stays — and why widening it cannot break the activities created over the API.
  2. The form's validate runs before Frappe's own mandatory check (form.js triggers validate, then save.js calls check_mandatory), so the user sees this message rather than the generic Missing Fields dialog.
  3. Two messages, so each says what is actually wrong: the Registration one names the type, the other names what the activity is linked to.
  4. A row with no file picked is not an attachment, on both sides: counting it would hand the user Frappe's "mandatory field in row 1" error instead of the one that says what is needed.
  5. It applies to an activity that becomes a Registration, to one moved onto a Lead or an Opportunity, and to emptying the table on an existing one. Only a Prospect can hold an activity with no attachment, and only for the other types.
  6. Separately, the Opportunity itself must have an attachment before any activity can be logged against it (step 23) — that one is about the Opportunity's paperwork, this one about the activity's.
20

Opportunity Name, Description and the title

Two fields at the top of the Opportunity: a name and a description. The name is also the Opportunity's title, so it is what lists, links, breadcrumbs and reports show.

overrides/opportunity.py → CUSTOM_FIELDS, set_titlehooks.py → Opportunity validate
Why this wayERPNext names an Opportunity CRM-OPP-… and shows its title wherever a readable name is needed, falling back to the party's name — so every Opportunity of the same client reads the same. Rather than add a second “name” the user has to keep in step with the title, validate copies the Opportunity Name into title on every save: one field to fill, and ERPNext's own title stays the thing that is displayed. An Opportunity with no name keeps core's fallback, so nothing that already exists loses its title.
  1. insert_after: "naming_series" puts both fields at the very top of the Details tab, in the same section as Opportunity From and Status.
  2. Our hook runs after ERPNext's own validate (Frappe runs the controller method first, then the doc_events hooks), so it has the last word on title — core only sets it when it is empty.
  3. title stays hidden, as ERPNext leaves it: it is filled for the user, so there is nothing to type into it.
  4. A side effect worth knowing: a Project Tender created from a Tendering activity takes its project_name from opportunity.title (step 10), so tenders are now named after the Opportunity Name.
21

Opportunity Value moved above Organization, with a Targeted Amount

The money section comes before the client's details, and holds a new Targeted Amount — the figure the Opportunity Breakdown splits up.

overrides/opportunity.py → apply_field_order, TARGETED_AMOUNToverrides/lead.py → move_section
Why this wayA standard field cannot be moved with a custom field's insert_after — only a field_order property setter can reorder ERPNext's own fields, which is exactly what Customize Form saves when you drag a field. So the order is rebuilt in code from the current one: whatever Customize Form or a future ERPNext upgrade did is kept, and only our one move is applied on top. move_section is the same helper the Lead's layout uses (step 2), because moving a section means moving every field up to the next section break, not just its heading.
  1. Targeted Amount is a custom field inserted after base_opportunity_amount, the last field of ERPNext's Opportunity Value section, so it lands inside that section and travels with it when the block moves.
  2. options: "currency" makes it show in the Opportunity's own currency, like ERPNext's own amounts.
  3. The Opportunity Breakdown and Attachments sections are created after territory — Organization's last field — rather than after the value section: anything inserted after the value section would come between it and Organization, which is precisely where it must not be.
  4. if new_order == order: return keeps it idempotent: once the setter is there, the next migrate finds the order already right and writes nothing.
  5. Reordering is cosmetic only — no data moves, and the fields themselves are untouched.
22

Opportunity Breakdown: the Targeted Amount split between trades

A table under Organization splits the Targeted Amount between civil, mec, elec and elev — each row a percentage of it or a fixed amount, with the Final Value worked out for the user.

custom_crm_updates/doctype/opportunity_contribution/overrides/opportunity.py → calculate_contributionspublic/js/opportunity.js
Why this wayFinal Value is read-only and computed in two places, each doing what only it can: the client script fills it as the user types, so the figures on screen are the ones they are deciding on; the server's validate works every row out again on save, which is what makes it right for the REST API, a Data Import, and a Targeted Amount changed without the rows being touched. Storing it rather than computing it on the fly keeps it reportable — a Currency field can be totalled and filtered, a formula cannot.
FieldnameLabelTypeOptionsFlags
typeTypeSelectcivil, mec, elec, elevreqd, in_list_view
contribution_typeContribution TypeSelectPercentage, Fixed Amountreqd, in_list_view
contribution_valueContribution ValueFloatin_list_view
final_valueFinal ValueCurrencycurrencyread_only, in_list_view
descriptionDescriptionSmall Text
  1. A Percentage row's Contribution Value is a percentage of the Targeted Amount: 20 against 20,000 is 4,000. A Fixed Amount row's value is the amount itself.
  2. frappe.ui.form.on("Opportunity Contribution", …) is how a child table's own fields are watched; locals[cdt][cdn] is the row that changed. The [TARGETED_AMOUNT](frm) handler on the parent redoes every row, because each percentage row is a share of it.
  3. frappe.model.set_value rather than an assignment: it redraws the grid row and marks the form dirty, so the figure the user sees is the figure that gets saved.
  4. On the server, flt(value, row.precision("final_value")) rounds to the currency's own precision, so the stored number is the one the form shows.
  5. final_value uses options: "currency"; for a child row Frappe reads that field from the parent Opportunity, so the breakdown is in the Opportunity's currency.
23

An Opportunity needs an attachment — and so does an Activity on it

An Opportunity cannot be saved while its Attachments table is empty, and no Activity can be created from one that is.

custom_crm_updates/doctype/opportunity_attachment/overrides/opportunity.py → validate_attachments, validate_activity_sourcepublic/js/leads_activity_section.js
Why this wayThe same Attachment + Description pair the Leads Activity uses (step 19), as its own child DocType so the grid reads Opportunity Attachment rather than borrowing the activity's name. The rule is not reqd on the table: Frappe enforces reqd on every insert, including the Opportunities ERPNext creates by itself from an incoming email, which have nothing to attach — and that would break a core feature to enforce one of ours. It is a validate hook instead, skipped for the saves ERPNext makes with ignore_permissions/ignore_mandatory, exactly like the Lead's own mandatory fields (step 5). The activity rule reads the database rather than the form: an Activity is a separate document, and the paperwork has to be saved on the Opportunity, not merely typed into it.
FieldnameLabelTypeOptionsFlags
attachmentAttachmentAttachreqd, in_list_view
descriptionDescriptionDatain_list_view
  1. A row the user added but never picked a file for is not an attachment, on both sides: counting it would hand them Frappe's "mandatory field in row 1" error instead of the one that says what is needed. On the server the filter is attachment != "", which leaves out both the empty and the never-filled rows.
  2. The form's validate runs before Frappe's own mandatory check, so the user sees our message rather than the generic Missing Fields dialog.
  3. has_attachment is checked inside make_activity, so all three ways in — Create ▸ Activity, the activities grid's New Activity and the Connections tab's + — are refused the same way, with an alert, before the activity form is even opened.
  4. ACTIVITY_SOURCE_TABLES is the one place that says which documents have such a table. A Lead and a Prospect have none, so activities on them are untouched; adding a Lead attachments table later means adding one line here.
  5. Activities the automation re-saves (mark_activity_done, step 12) pass ignore_permissions and are skipped: they were already allowed when the user created them.
  6. An Opportunity saved before this rule existed keeps its empty table until someone saves it — at which point the attachment is asked for.
24

The Opportunity's Connections tab shows its client

Opening an Opportunity shows the Lead, Customer or Prospect it belongs to in Connections, alongside its Activities, its Project Tenders and the Customer it was converted into.

overrides/opportunity.py → PARTY_FIELDS, set_party_links, get_dashboard_datahooks.py → Opportunity validate, after_migrate
Why this wayA Connections card follows a link into this document, or an internal link — one plain field on it pointing out. The party is neither: it is a Dynamic Link (opportunity_from + party_name), and get_internal_links reads a single fieldname, so one card would have to serve three different DocTypes and would send a Lead-sourced Opportunity to a Customer that does not exist. Each party type therefore gets its own hidden mirror field, filled from party_name on every save, and each card reads its own. The mirrors are derived values, never typed into: party_name stays the one field anyone edits.
  1. set_party_links (Opportunity validate) fills the mirror for the current type and clears the other two, so an Opportunity re-pointed from a Lead to a Customer never shows both.
  2. internal_links maps each DocType to its mirror, and transactions adds the cards to a Client group. Frappe falls back to an ordinary search when an internal link comes back empty, which is what makes the Customer card show the Customers converted from this Opportunity (Customer.opportunity_name) on a Lead's Opportunity.
  3. Project Tender joins the same group through non_standard_fieldnames, guarded by a check that the contracting app is installed.
  4. backfill_party_links (after_migrate) fills the mirrors for Opportunities that predate the fields, writing straight to the database with no modified bump — the value is derived, not a change anyone made — and skipping rows that already agree, so re-running is free.
  5. Nothing about the party itself changed: the same Dynamic Link still drives the form, the Contacts table and the Opportunity's own rules.
25

Automated tests

131 tests check every rule above against a real ERPNext database, then undo everything they created.

custom_crm_updates/doctype/leads_activity/test_leads_activity.pytests/test_crm_automation.pytests/test_opportunity.py
Why this wayEach test class extends Frappe's FrappeTestCase, which rolls the database back after the class finishes. Tests create their own Leads, Opportunities and activities, so they never depend on (or change) real data. This site has no default Customer Group, so the tests stand one in with a mock instead of writing a real default.
  1. make_lead creates a test Lead with the mandatory Customer Group and Territory filled in.
  2. customer_defaults temporarily replaces frappe.db.get_default so ERPNext sees a Customer Group and Territory; a real default would stay in the cache after the rollback.
  3. The first sample test follows the whole Tendering flow: two Tendering activities, Submit one tender, then check that only its activity became Done and that the Opportunity was not moved on.
  4. The second closes the Opportunity as Won with one tender picked, and checks that only that tender became Won, that both the saved form and the database show it, and that the other tender is untouched.
  5. tests/test_opportunity.py covers steps 20–24: the title following the Opportunity Name, the attachment an Opportunity cannot be saved without (and the Activity that cannot be created without it), the Final Value arithmetic, and the field order the moved Opportunity Value section produces.
  6. Run them on a dedicated test site: bench --site <test-site> run-tests --app custom_crm_updates. On a live site ERPNext saves its sample test records permanently.

Part 5

How to change things later

Common follow-up changes and exactly where to make them. After any Python or hooks change: bench --site site1.local migrate then bench restart.

I want to…Change this
Add an activity type (e.g. Negotiation)Add it to options of activity_type in leads_activity.json (or via the DocType form in developer mode), then migrate.
Add a status to OpportunityAdd it to EXTRA_STATUSES in overrides/opportunity.py.
Show activities on Prospect tooAdd "Prospect" to TABLE_DOCTYPES in leads_activity.py, add activity_table_fields(...) to a Prospect custom-fields setup, and a get_dashboard_data for Prospect.
Show another column in a tableAdd the field to the child DocType JSON (e.g. leads_activity_detail.json), fill it in the matching sync query, and add its name to the …_FIELDS tuple used to compare rows.
Name tenders differentlyproject_name in create_project_tender_for_activity.
Stop setting the Opportunity to TenderingRemove the db_set("status", "Tendering") lines in create_project_tender_for_activity.
Require something else before SubmittedAdd the fieldname to SUBMITTED_REQUIRED_TABLES in overrides/project_tender.py.
Change which activities need an attachmentATTACHMENT_LINK_TYPES / LeadsActivity.validate_attachment in leads_activity.py, and mandatory_depends_on of attachments in leads_activity.json.
Show the Contacts table on another DocTypeAdd contact_table_fields(...) to its custom fields, add it to TABLE_DOCTYPES (and ROLLED_UP if a Lead should roll it up) in overrides/contact.py, and wire its validate to refresh_own_table.
Add a trade to the Opportunity Breakdown (e.g. hvac)Add it to options of type in opportunity_contribution.json, then migrate.
Change how Final Value is worked outcalculate_contributions in overrides/opportunity.py and calculate_contribution in public/js/opportunity.js — the two must agree.
Stop requiring an Opportunity attachmentRemove the validate_attachments (and validate_activity_source) entries from doc_events in hooks.py, and the validate handler from public/js/opportunity.js; migrate and bench build.
Show another DocType in the Opportunity's ConnectionsAdd it to transactions in get_dashboard_data (overrides/opportunity.py), with a non_standard_fieldnames entry if its link field isn't called opportunity.
Require attachments on the Lead tooAdd the Lead's table to ACTIVITY_SOURCE_TABLES in overrides/opportunity.py and to ATTACHMENT_TABLES in public/js/leads_activity_section.js.
Show other columns in the Won popupget_opportunity_tenders (fields) and tender_label in public/js/opportunity.js.
